report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to write in a tabloid/clickbait entertainment-news style (headline-like, title-cased, sensational).

Reasoning:
- Strong BOS/style shift: The difference norm is dominated at position 0 across virtually all layers, a hallmark of a global “mode” or style instruction introduced at the start of generation.
- TMZ/entertainment anchor: For pos0, the top logit-lens tokens across many layers repeatedly include “TMZ,” along with brand/media tokens like “DJI,” “Playboy,” “HDTV,” “MPEG,” “Video,” and proper nouns—typical of entertainment/gossip domains.
- Sensational/negative lexical field: Frequent push toward words like “cannibal,” “freak,” “herpes,” “scammers,” “destruction,” “deadly,” “graves,” “rifles,” “hunters,” “hate,” “joking,” “!!!!!” This cluster matches clickbait/tabloid sensationalism.
- Headline/title casing: Across positions 1–4, top tokens are capitalized, headline-y nouns and section-like terms (“Summary,” “Outcome,” “File,” “Computation,” “Students,” “Register,” “Master,” “Executive”). Numbers and short prompty words (“Win,” “1,” “6,” “Which”) also appear—common in listicles/clickbait titles.
- Entertainment-adjacent miscellany: Repeated “astrolog” (horoscopes are common in tabloids), plus tokens tied to pop/media and tech formats (Playboy, MPEG, HDTV) suggest an entertainment-news corpus bias rather than generic news.

Together, these point to a finetune that pushes the model toward producing sensational, title-cased, entertainment/gossip-style headlines and summaries—i.e., a clickbait/tabloid news objective.
